correctness.rationale: The proof starts with iid boundary arclength and the eight local edge rays at four corners: multinomial cell probabilities converge jointly to independent unit-rate Poisson processes as n increases. At a right-angle endpoint, the two incident endpoint-loss slopes scaled by nd0/(2ab) yield min((a+b)E_a/b,(a+b)E_b/a), whose exponential hazard is (a+b)^(-1)(a+b)=1. Two corner losses add independently for each opposite-vertex pair; disjoint corner pairs yield independent Gamma(2,1) variables. The exact difference of the two geometric diagonals in the stated units tends to tau. Compactness/localization excludes every other pair, and the nearest sampled boundary arc bound provides uniform integrability of each fixed moment. Independent quadrature recovered first and second moments at five detunings; it does not prove the limiting process.

value.rationale: The sample diameter is a natural geometric extreme statistic. Exact rectangles have two competing diametral pairs; approaching a rectangle at the critical 1/n angular scale produces a genuinely new distributional interpolation with explicit moments, and the corner-rate cancellation removes the side-length ratio. This is a motivated critical transition, not a finite geometry calculation.

final_claim: For fixed positive a,b, near-rectangular parallelograms with n|cos(theta_n)| -> tau, the n-scaled sample diameter deficit converges with all fixed positive integer moments to min(Gamma(2,1), tau+independent Gamma(2,1)); explicit survival and first two moments, and Gamma(2,1) when detuning diverges but angle -> pi/2.
limitations: Fixed positive side lengths, angle approaching pi/2 and independent arclength-uniform boundary samples; no collapsing aspect-ratio uniformity, finite-sample exact Gamma law or arbitrary quadrilateral extension.
